synopsis: VIL drives a complete real machine in a safe test area with virtual hazards, allowing real braking dynamics, controller and actuator delays, latency and operator-interface behaviour to be tested without endangering people or targets [f13388, f5333]. It does not establish perception of injected objects unless sensors are stimulated over the air, and fidelity remains constrained by stimulation, testbench dynamics and simulated versus real ground interaction [f5335, f940]. The 2024 on-road survey reports costly, variably accurate systems and no full-scale platform ready for comprehensive industrial testing; no complete heavy-off-road automatic-braking VIL case was found, although vendor material describes real-tractor VIL [f341, f5340, f342, f8652]. The recommended hierarchy uses SIL for volume, HIL for timing, interfaces and faults, VIL only where added physical fidelity justifies investment, and real machines for stopping, terrain and environmental evidence [f13313]. Accordingly, a team starting from zero in October 2026 should not promise a complete multi-sensor heavy-off-road VIL facility by mid-2027, and the programme's economic justification remains uncertain [f866, f1119].
